the governance of the Shari’ah Supervisory Board of Islamic banks and how it affects the risk taking behavior of the bank’s loan portfolio.

the SSB is an important factor for the risk taking behavior of Islamic banks.

SSB composition characteristics have a strong influence on the risk taking behavior of the loan portfolio of the Islamic banks.
the risk taking behavior of Islamic banks is influenced by the composition of the Shari’ah Supervisory Board.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Islamic banks are not less risky in comparison to conventional banks, but that the SSBs are less effective in monitoring risk taking behavior in the loan portfolio.
Islamic banks' risk taking is influenced by SSB composition factors.
the SSBs are not effective in their supervisory role, which is due to their decentralized governance structure, and that they should be restructured to a more centralized governance model.
